stated: The Conservative Party will introduce mandatory National Service for all school leavers at 18, offering a choice between a competitive year-long military placement or 25 days a year of civic service roles, backed by a Royal Commission and funding rising to £2.5 billion.

source.quote: Give young people the skills and opportunities they deserve by introducing mandatory National Service for all school leavers at 18, with the choice between a competitive placement in the military or civic service roles.

bearing_set.reason: A military-placement track and a £2.5 bn programme directly affects UK defence capacity, trained-personnel pipeline, and national security posture — a real verdict on safety/security is unavoidable.

Mandatory participation at 18 materially disrupts the transition from school to further education, university, or skilled employment, with non-negligible effects on opportunity and skills development for every cohort.

Legal compulsion on all 18-year-olds to perform state-directed service (even with two options) is a substantive civil-liberties question — a genuine verdict on freedom from compelled service is warranted.

A mandatory year-long military placement removes 18-year-olds from the labour market entirely, plausibly reducing employment rates and delaying wage-growth trajectories for that cohort; civic service (25 days/year) is a lesser but still concrete displacement.
Compulsory participation for all school leavers is a state mandate over bodily autonomy and freedom from coercion — the clearest possible O10 bearing, regardless of the 'choice' between routes.
A £2.5bn (rising) new spending commitment must be funded or borrowed; this materially affects the debt-sustainability path and earns a genuine O12 verdict.
Civic service is explicitly designed to build inter-group contact, social trust and belonging across socioeconomic lines — the indicators O15 is defined by — earning a real verdict there.

membership_note: Five fundamentals: the policy is genuinely multi-dimensional — it imposes a coercive mandate (O10), builds defence capacity (O5), targets social cohesion (O15), disrupts early educational/career pathways (O7), and carries a material new fiscal commitment (O12). Each has a specific, nameable mechanism and indicator.
